note: the release-delta lens: same board, two official releases 4.5 years apart, diffed at FFS-body granularity (sha256_16 of file body). What does a BIOS update actually change?
identity_rule: hash of the FFS file BODY (all sections concatenated as walked) — the header carries size/state bits that churn without content change

name_join.lesson: the ring-13 packaging lens holds: ASUS ships 384 VERSION sections and ONE UI section, so the two ROMs alone cannot name their modules — the quorum boards lend their voices

reading.churn: 46.3% of the GUID set is byte-identical across 4.5 years; the changed majority is AMD platform silicon support (AmdApcb*/AmdCcx*/AmdCpm* — the AGESA family), exactly the modules a vendor must rebuild per AGESA update
reading.security_growth: the 7 added modules are ASUS flash protection: PrepareWhiteListSmm, SbRomArmorSmm, FlashSmiSmm, FlashSmiDxe (+2 unnamed SMM/DXE) — the vendor's own flash-attack hardening appearing between 2022 and 2026
reading.nvram_cross_check: the NVRAM store file (CEF5B9A3-476D-497F-9FDC-E98143E0422C, the ring-14 anchor) changes content at identical size 130,952 B — factory defaults moved; the delta lens re-derives the ring-14 finding independently
reading.one_byte: 1DF36FF9-… 80,232 -> 80,231 B — a one-byte content change in a 78-KiB blob; body-hash identity sees it, size comparison never would

honesty: body-hash identity ignores FFS header/state bits by design; a module could change only its header and be called unchanged (never observed, not proven impossible)
two releases measured; no claim about the 37 intermediate releases between 3604 and 4655
AGESA version strings stay shallow ('AGESA Driver' only) — the AGESA level per release is not recovered by this lens
names are a 532-GUID join, not this board's own UI voice
